descriptionChirho: To devote to complete destruction as an act of divine judgment or holy war, annihilating persons, cities, or nations under the ban (herem).
To dedicate or consecrate something irrevocably to the LORD, setting it apart as devoted property rather than destroying it.
To cause to dry up or become desolate, a distinct sense evidenced by multilingual glosses indicating drying or withering rather than destruction.
To place under a curse or ban (anathema), prohibiting contact or use, with the focus on the act of banning rather than physical annihilation.
Hofal passive: to be subjected to the ban of complete destruction, utterly annihilated by divine decree.
Hofal passive: to be set apart as irrevocably devoted or consecrated to the LORD, without implication of destruction.
Hofal passive: to have property seized or forfeited, confiscated under legal or religious authority as a penalty.
